worked_example.problem: How can Bih get clean salt from a mixture of salt and sand?
steps: Add water and stir: the salt dissolves, the sand does not.
Filter: the sand stays on the filter paper; salt water (the filtrate) passes through.
Evaporate the water from the filtrate: salt crystals are left.
worked_example.answer: Dissolve in water, filter, then evaporate the filtrate.

cards.idea: Use a difference: size (sieving), colour or size you can see (hand-picking), magnetism (magnet), weight (winnowing).
example: A magnet pulls iron filings out of sand.

cards.idea: If one solid sublimes (iodine, ammonium chloride), heat the mixture and collect it as it cools.
example: Iodine turns into a purple gas and forms crystals again on a cold surface.

cards.idea: If one solid dissolves and the other does not: dissolve, filter, then evaporate.
example: Salt and sand → salt water + sand → salt crystals.

pick.why: To separate stones from rice, use hand-picking.
To separate fine garri from lumps, use sieving.
To separate iron filings from sand, use magnetic separation.
To separate chaff from rice grains, use winnowing.
To separate iodine from sand, use sublimation.
To separate salt from sand, use dissolving, filtering and evaporating.

questions.prompt: Which method would you use to separate {x.t}?

misconceptions.explain: That method uses a different difference between the solids.

questions.prompt: Match each method with how it works.

pool.right: pick out the unwanted pieces by hand
shake through a sieve: small pieces fall through, big ones stay
a magnet pulls out the iron
the wind blows away the light chaff
heat: one solid turns into a gas and is collected when it cools
dissolve one solid, filter out the other, evaporate the water

questions.prompt: Put the steps in order to get salt from a mixture of salt and sand.

items.text: Add water and stir until the salt dissolves.
Collect the salt water (filtrate) in an evaporating dish.
Heat until the water evaporates and salt is left.

questions.prompt: Why can a magnet separate iron filings from sand?

right.text: Iron is attracted by a magnet; sand is not.

wrong.explain: Weight is not used here; magnetism is.
Iron does not dissolve in water.

wrong.text: Sand is attracted by a magnet.
wrong.explain: Sand is not attracted; iron is.

questions.prompt: One sentence is wrong. Which one?

right.text: Winnowing removes the light chaff from grain.
Sieving separates pieces of different sizes.
Iodine can be separated from sand by sublimation.

wrong.text: A magnet separates salt from sand.
wrong.explain: Neither salt nor sand is magnetic: dissolve, filter and evaporate.
Their grains are the same size; sieving cannot separate them.
